subject: entomology
intro: Entomology leads to work with the most numerous animals on Earth — studying insects in the wild and the lab, managing the pests that hit crops and buildings, and reading the insects found at crime scenes.

roles.title: Zoologists and Wildlife Biologists
roles.what: Study the origins, behaviour, diseases, genetics and life processes of animals and wildlife, collecting and analysing biological data to determine the environmental effects of present and potential land and water uses.
roles.where: The insect evolution and anatomy unit, metamorphosis and life-cycle strategies, and insect ecology and behaviour — coevolution, social insects, pollination and food webs — are the zoologist's toolkit applied to the largest animal phylum.

roles.title: Soil and Plant Scientists
roles.what: Conduct research on crop breeding, physiology, yield and management, and on controlling pests — or study soil composition as it relates to plant growth and the effects of alternative practices on productivity.
roles.where: The applied entomology unit's pest management and IPM topic is literally the job's core problem, backed by plant–insect coevolution and pollination ecology from the insect ecology unit.

roles.title: Pest Control Workers
roles.what: Apply or release chemical solutions or toxic gases, and set traps, to kill or remove pests and vermin that infest buildings and the areas around them.
roles.where: Knowing the enemy is the trade: metamorphosis and life cycles explain where larvae hide, the major orders unit trains identification of cockroaches, termites and ants, and IPM frames why bait and exclusion beat blanket spraying.

roles.title: Forensic Science Technicians
roles.what: Collect, identify, classify and analyse physical evidence from criminal investigations, run tests on substances such as tissue and fibre, and may testify in court as expert witnesses.
roles.where: The forensic insects topic from applied entomology — colonisation stages and insect succession as a body's clock — plus anatomy and metamorphosis training, feed straight into entomology's best-known forensic speciality.

roles.title: Conservation Scientists
roles.what: Manage, improve and protect natural resources to maximise their use without damaging the environment, advising land users on practices that conserve soil, water and habitat.
roles.where: Pollination and food webs, insects as beneficial organisms, and plant–insect coevolution from the ecology unit give conservation scientists the pollinator and biodiversity expertise habitat management increasingly needs.
